title: Ratio Problems and Best Buys
seo_title: Year 9 Ratio Problems Worksheets: Sharing in a Ratio, Best Buys and Combining Ratios
standard_code: KS3: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
standard_text: Divide a given quantity into two parts in a given part : part or part : whole ratio; express the division of a quantity into two parts as a ratio; solve problems involving direct and inverse proportion; use compound units such as unit pricing.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 ratio problems worksheets: share in a ratio with three parts, problems with a difference or one share, best buys by unit price, combining ratios and recipes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Find the value of one part first.
key_sub: Best buy: compare the price for the same amount.
body_html:
How it works

To share in a ratio, add the parts, find one part, then multiply. If you know a difference or one share, find what one part is worth first.

For a best buy, compare the price for the same amount (per 100 g, per litre or per item). To combine a : b and b : c, make the b parts the same.

Example

Share £120 in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.

6 parts, one part = £20.

Answer: £20, £40, £60

Example

Ratio 3 : 7. The second share is £28 more.

4 parts = £28, so one part = £7.

Answer: £21 and £49

Example

500 g for £2.50 or 750 g for £3.60?

50p and 48p per 100 g.

Answer: 750 g is better value

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by the number of people instead of the number of parts.
  • Mixing up which share goes with which person.
  • Choosing the cheapest pack instead of the best value per unit.
  • Adding the middle numbers when combining ratios instead of making them equal.

faq.q: How do I share an amount in a ratio?
faq.a: Add the parts of the ratio, divide the amount by that total to find one part, then multiply by each number in the ratio.

faq.q: How do I solve a ratio problem when I know the difference?
faq.a: Subtract the parts of the ratio. That number of parts equals the difference, so you can find one part.

faq.q: How do I find the best buy?
faq.a: Work out the price for the same amount of each, such as per 100 g. The lower price per unit is the better value.

faq.q: How do I combine two ratios?
faq.a: For a : b and b : c, multiply so the b values match, then write a : b : c.

items.q: Ruby, Maya and Kai share £27 in the ratio 5 : 3 : 1. How much does Kai get?
items.e: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 parts. One part = £27 ÷ 9 = £3. Kai gets 1 × £3 = £3.

items.q: Theo and Harry share some sweets in the ratio 1 : 3. Harry gets 16 more sweets than Theo. How many sweets are there altogether?
items.e: The difference is 3 − 1 = 2 parts = 16, so one part = 8. Total = 4 parts = 32.

items.q: Money is shared between Arjun and Ava in the ratio 4 : 7. Arjun gets £28. How much does Ava get?

items.q: a : b = 5 : 5 and b : c = 3 : 3. Write a : b : c as a ratio in its simplest form.
items.e: Make the b parts equal: the LCM of 5 and 3 is 15. 15 : 15 and 15 : 15 give 1 : 1 : 1.

items.q: Red and blue counters are in the ratio 3 : 2. What fraction of the counters are red?

items.q: Concrete is made from cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 1 : 2 : 4. How much sand is in 350 kg of concrete?
items.e: 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 parts. One part = 50 kg. Sand: 2 × 50 = 100 kg.

items.q: Ages of Amelia and her grandad are in the ratio 2 : 11. Grandad is 66. How old is Amelia?

items.q: The ratio of red to green sweets is 2 : 5. After 4 red sweets are eaten, the ratio is 1 : 5. How many green sweets are there?
items.e: Green stays the same. Red goes from 2 parts to 1 part, so 1 part = 4 sweets. Green: 5 × 4 = 20.

items.q: Paint is mixed blue to yellow in the ratio 3 : 2. Jack has 9 litres of blue. How much yellow does he need?
